trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, Gwalior in case No.10697/2020 RCSHM
case_name: Smt. Deepa Tomar vs Ajay @ Leeladhar Singh Tomar
facts_of_case: The parties were married on 21.11.2011 and had a baby girl named Bhumi. The petitioner claimed that the respondent was cruel, aggressive, and short-tempered, and sought dissolution of marriage under Section 13(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act.

legal_principles.principle: Mental cruelty can be caused by a husband's criminal background and uncertainty of his release on bail.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, no wife can live in the matrimonial relationship with the person who is so short-tempered and impulsive turned criminal.

legal_principles.principle: Desertion can be situational, and a wife may be entitled to divorce if her husband has been absent for more than two years.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, this is the situational desertion of wife by the respondent/husband.
use_in: divorce cases involving long-term absence of husbands

outcome.final_order: The petition filed by the petitioner seeking dissolution of marriage was dismissed by the trial court. The appeal is also dismissed.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for dissolution of marriage under Section 13 (1) Hindu Marriage Act
